articles.title: Free trade pact with EU expected soon, to boost textile industry: Vice President
articles.source: Business News Today: Latest Business New
articles.summary: The Indian Vice President stated that a free trade agreement with the EU is expected soon, aimed at boosting the textile industry.
articles.explain: A Free Trade Agreement is an arrangement between countries or blocs to reduce or eliminate taxes (tariffs) on imported and exported goods. By lowering these costs, Indian products like textiles become more competitive in European markets. This potentially drives industrial growth and job creation in major Indian manufacturing hubs.

story.title: India-EU Free Trade Prospects
story.so_far: India and the European Union have been engaged in prolonged negotiations for a Free Trade Agreement (FTA) to lower tariffs and simplify trade. The Indian government has prioritized this as a way to integrate domestic industries, especially manufacturing, into the global value chain.

timeline.text: New official statements suggest a near-term conclusion to trade negotiations between India and the EU, with a focus on textiles.

articles.title: Binance says customer withdrawals are fully restored, four weeks after the $6.3 billion hack
articles.source: CoinDesk: Bitcoin, Ethereum, Crypto News
articles.summary: Binance has restored all customer withdrawals after a massive $6.3 billion hack occurred last month.
articles.explain: A crypto exchange is a digital marketplace where users buy and sell cryptocurrencies. When a hack occurs, the exchange must freeze activity to stop further theft and verify the integrity of the remaining balances. Restoring withdrawals indicates that the platform has secured its systems and confirmed user account data is safe.

related.title: Binance says phase one of withdrawals opens after $6.3B hack

story.title: Binance $6.3 Billion Security Breach
story.so_far: In late October 2026, the global cryptocurrency exchange Binance suffered a major security breach resulting in the loss of $6.3 billion in assets. Following the incident, the platform paused withdrawals to investigate and secure user funds, gradually phasing in restores over the month of November.

timeline.text: The breach was officially confirmed as the largest crypto hack to date.
Binance is actively investigating the breach and has pledged to cover user losses while security firms link the activity to North Korean actors.
The breach continues to evolve as further vulnerabilities are identified within the exchange's infrastructure.
TRM Labs has identified potential links between the theft and North Korea-affiliated hackers.
Technical analysis suggests the Ethereum upgrade EIP-7702 likely facilitated the bypass of withdrawal safeguards.
The stolen funds total over 18,000 BTC and 500,000 ETH, surpassing the corporate reserves of major competitors like Coinbase.
Binance announced a plan to cover losses for customers after a $6.3 billion cyberattack targeted the exchange's digital assets.
The exchange has begun the process of allowing users to withdraw their funds again, starting with Bitcoin, as part of its recovery efforts.
Investigators have identified the North Korean group 'TraderTraitor' as the culprit behind the massive theft.
The FBI has officially blamed North Korea for the $6.3 billion theft, while Binance confirms the first phase of withdrawal services is live.
The platform has finalized the recovery process, returning full access to customers.
The exchange has fully resumed normal operations and withdrawal capabilities four weeks after the incident.

articles.title: Standard Chartered's Zodia Custody suffers data breach, exposing client information
articles.source: CoinDesk: Bitcoin, Ethereum, Crypto News
articles.summary: Zodia Custody, a crypto firm backed by Standard Chartered, has reported a data breach that compromised client information.
articles.explain: A data breach occurs when unauthorized individuals gain access to sensitive or private information stored by a company. Zodia Custody acts as a 'digital vault' for institutions, so this breach highlights the persistent risks involved in securing digital assets against increasingly sophisticated cyberattacks.

story.title: Zodia Custody Data Breach
story.so_far: Zodia Custody is an institutional-grade crypto asset custodian supported by banking giant Standard Chartered. Cybersecurity remains a critical concern for such firms, as they hold the keys to significant digital assets on behalf of corporate and institutional clients.

timeline.text: Zodia Custody confirmed a security incident involving unauthorized access to client data.

articles.title: Tether can freeze stolen crypto in minutes. Getting it back can take years.
articles.source: CoinDesk: Bitcoin, Ethereum, Crypto News
articles.summary: While Tether can quickly freeze stolen stablecoins on its network, recovering the funds for users is often a lengthy legal process.
articles.explain: Tether is a stablecoin designed to maintain a 1:1 value with the US dollar. Because it is centralized, the company can blacklist specific digital wallet addresses if the tokens are flagged as stolen. However, legal systems struggle to process these digital recoveries because crypto transactions are pseudonymous and span multiple international borders.

story.title: Challenges in Stolen Crypto Recovery
story.so_far: Stablecoin issuers like Tether maintain centralized control over their tokens, allowing them to blacklist addresses associated with hacks or money laundering. However, simply freezing the assets does not equate to immediate restitution for victims, as complex jurisdictional and legal battles usually follow.

timeline.text: Analysts highlight the disparity between the speed of freezing illicit crypto and the duration of legal asset recovery.

articles.title: Gold ETFs vs Gold Mutual Funds: Amid ups and downs in rates, which is better instrument to buy for good returns?
articles.source: mint - markets
articles.summary: Investors are comparing Gold ETFs and Gold Mutual Funds as strategies to manage market volatility.
articles.explain: Gold ETFs (Exchange Traded Funds) are gold-backed securities that trade on stock exchanges like stocks, meaning they require a 'demat' (dematerialized) account to hold. Gold mutual funds invest in these ETFs or gold mining stocks, offering an alternative for those without direct stock market access.

story.title: Gold Investment Vehicles Comparison
story.so_far: As interest rates fluctuate, investors often turn to gold as a hedge against inflation and market uncertainty. Choosing the right vehicle depends on the investor's access to trading infrastructure and their tolerance for transaction fees.

timeline.text: Market analysis highlights that Gold ETFs are cost-effective but require a demat account, unlike some mutual fund alternatives.

articles.title: Gold vs silver: Precious metals prices crashed and rebounded - which of them could deliver better returns in 2027?
articles.source: mint - markets
articles.summary: Gold and silver prices have both dropped in November due to a strengthening US dollar and higher bond yields.
articles.explain: Non-yielding assets like gold and silver do not pay interest or dividends. When US Treasury bonds offer high interest rates, investors prefer holding those bonds for guaranteed returns rather than holding gold, causing precious metal prices to decline.

story.title: Precious Metals Market Correction
story.so_far: Precious metals are often inversely correlated to the US dollar and interest rates. As US monetary policy tightens and bond yields rise, these non-yielding assets become less attractive to investors, leading to broad market sell-offs.

timeline.text: In November, gold futures dropped 13% and silver fell 20% on the domestic market.

articles.title: ESMA to overhaul EU’s MiCA crypto register in 2027
articles.source: Cointelegraph.com News
articles.summary: The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) is planning to modernize the EU's crypto regulatory register by 2027.
articles.explain: A 'white paper' in crypto is a document explaining the technology and economic model behind a new digital asset. MiCA is the first major set of laws in Europe that creates a clear legal structure for crypto companies, and ESMA is the regulatory body tasked with ensuring these companies follow European financial standards.

story.title: EU Crypto Regulatory Overhaul
story.so_far: MiCA (Markets in Crypto-Assets) is the EU's comprehensive regulatory framework designed to standardize the crypto industry. Regulators are now focusing on improving the technical infrastructure needed to enforce these rules, including how companies report their white papers and operational history.

timeline.text: A new automated MiCA register will replace current manual processes to improve data accuracy and reporting.
